# RealWorld Backend API

A [RealWorld](https://realworld-docs.netlify.app/) backend implementation built with
**TypeScript (Node.js) + Fastify + Prisma + SQLite**.

It implements the full RealWorld backend specification: JWT authentication, users &
profiles, article CRUD, comments, favorites, tags, and the personalized feed.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18+ (developed on Node 24)
- [Hurl](https://hurl.dev) 4+ (only needed to run the API test suite)

## Getting started

Install dependencies and start the development server with a single command:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` automatically generates the Prisma client and syncs the SQLite schema
(`predev`), then boots the server on `http://localhost:8000`. All routes are served
under the `/api` prefix (e.g. `GET http://localhost:8000/api/tags`).

Configuration is read from `.env`:

| Variable       | Default                              | Description                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `file:./dev.db`                      | SQLite database location    |
| `JWT_SECRET`   | `realworld-dev-secret-change-me`     | Secret used to sign JWTs    |
| `PORT`         | `8000`                               | HTTP port                   |

## Project layout

```
prisma/schema.prisma   Data model (User, Article, Tag, Comment + relations)
src/
  server.ts            Entry point (listen)
  app.ts               Fastify instance, error handling, route registration
  auth.ts              JWT signing + auth preHandlers
  errors.ts            ApiError and RealWorld-shaped error helpers
  presenters.ts        Response serializers (user/profile/article/comment)
  prisma.ts            Prisma client singleton
  routes/              users, profiles, articles, comments, tags
specs/api/hurl/        Vendored official RealWorld Hurl test suite (13 files)
```

## API endpoints

Authentication uses the header `Authorization: Token <jwt>`.

- `POST   /api/users` — register
- `POST   /api/users/login` — login
- `GET    /api/user` — current user
- `PUT    /api/user` — update current user
- `GET    /api/profiles/:username` — get profile
- `POST   /api/profiles/:username/follow` — follow
- `DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow` — unfollow
- `GET    /api/articles` — list articles (`tag`, `author`, `favorited`, `limit`, `offset`)
- `GET    /api/articles/feed` — feed of followed authors
- `POST   /api/articles` — create article
- `GET    /api/articles/:slug` — get article
- `PUT    /api/articles/:slug` — update article
- `DELETE /api/articles/:slug` — delete article
- `POST   /api/articles/:slug/favorite` — favorite
- `DELETE /api/articles/:slug/favorite` — unfavorite
- `GET    /api/articles/:slug/comments` — list comments
- `POST   /api/articles/:slug/comments` — add comment
- `DELETE /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id` — delete comment
- `GET    /api/tags` — list tags

## Running the API tests

The official RealWorld Hurl collection is vendored under `specs/api/hurl/`
(13 files, 154 requests). With the server running:

```bash
npm run test:api
# or explicitly:
HOST=http://localhost:8000 bash specs/api/run-api-tests-hurl.sh
```

All 13 files / 154 requests pass.
